stem: In the Indian Fiscal federal system resources are allocated from the centre to the states, which of the following is not a means of resource allocation at present?

options.label: c

expl: In the Indian Fiscal Federal System, resources are from the Centre to the State. Transfer for plan implementation under the Gadgil formula is not a means of resource allocation at present. As per Article-280, the Finance Commission is constituted to make recommendations to the President about the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the Union and States (tax sharing). The centrally sponsored schemes and Grant-in-aid are also means of resource allocation from centre to states.

stem: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with the relations between the Union and the State?
expl: Part XI of the Indian Constitution deals with the Relations between the Union and the States. The Provisions of the part are divided into two parts, (i) Legislative Relations (Article 245-255) (ii) Administrative Relations (Article 256-263) Part-3 is the 'Fundamental Rights', Part-4 is the 'Directive Principles of State Policy’ and Part-6 is the 'States'.

stem: In which part of the Indian Constitution, legislative relations between Centre and States are given?
expl: The legislative relations between the Centre and States are given in Part XI of the Indian Constitution under Articles 245-255. Legislative subjects have been distributed among three lists of the seventh schedule, Union List – 97 subjects (At Present – 98) State List – 66 subjects (At Present – 59) Concurrent List – 47 subjects (At Present – 52)

stem: Indian Constitution presents three lists for the distribution of power between centre and states. Which two Articles regulate that distribution?
expl: Article 245 describes the extent of laws made by Parliament and by the Legislatures of States. According to Article 246(1)- Parliament has exclusive power to make laws with respect to any of the matters enumerated in List-I (Union List) in the Seventh Schedule. As per Article 246(2), Parliament and subject to clause(3), Legislature of any State also, has the power to make laws with respect to any of the matters enumerated in List III in the Seventh Schedule and according to Article 246(3), Subject to clause (1) and (2), the legislature of any State has exclusive power to make laws for such State or any part there of with respect to any of the matters enumerated in List II in the Seventh Schedule (State List), and according to Article 246(4), Parliament has the power to make laws with respect to any matter for any part of the territory of India not included in a State notwithstanding that such matter is a matter enumerated in the State List. Thus option (d) is correct.

stem: The distribution of legislative powers between the Centre and the States in the Constitution is given in –
expl: According to Article 246 of the Indian Constitution, all the provisions regarding relations between the Centre and States lie in the 7th Schedule of the Indian Constitution.

stem: Subjects on which centre and state both can make law are mentioned in which of the following Lists?
expl: The Union and the State can make laws on the subjects mentioned in the Concurrent list, but if there is any conflict in the laws made by the Union and State, the law made by the Union shall prevail.

stem: Which of the following is empowered to make law for economic and social planning besides the infants and minors in India?

expl: Economic and Social Planning and infants and minors subjects are on the Concurrent List. Both the Central and State Governments have the right to make laws on subjects of the Concurrent List. Thus, option (c) is the correct answer.

stem: Who is vested with the residuary powers in Indian Constitutions?
expl: According to Article 248 of the Indian Constitution, all the residuary legislative powers have been provided to the Parliament. Although, these are often provided to States in other federal setup as in the case of the U.S.A.

stem: What are Residuary subjects?

options.label: a
options.text: Subjects included in the State list

options.label: b
options.text: Subjects included in the Concurrent list

options.label: c
options.text: Subjects not included in any list

options.label: d
options.text: Subjects included in the Union list

expl: Residuary subjects refer to matters that are not specifically mentioned in the Union List, State List, or Concurrent List under the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution. These subjects emerge due to changing circumstances, advancements in technology, or new policy needs. According to Article 248, the Parliament of India has exclusive power to legislate on these matters, meaning only the Union Legislature can make laws regarding them. Examples of residuary subjects include cyber laws, space research, atomic energy, artificial intelligence regulations, and foreign trade policies, as these areas were not foreseen when the Constitution was drafted. As new challenges arise, Parliament retains the authority to govern such subjects.

stem: The Indian Constitution vests the residuary powers with:

options.label: d

expl: The Indian Constitution gives the residuary power of legislation to the Union Government. The Indian Union reflects the example of a strong Union where the residuary powers of legislation rest with the Parliament.

expl: Article 249 of the Indian Constitution is related to the legislative powers of the Parliament with respect to subjects in the State List in the national interest. This Article empowers the Parliament to make laws with respect to any matter enumerated in the State List.

stem: A resolution passed under clause (1) of Article 249 shall remain in force for a period not exceeding

expl: A resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha under Article 249 of the Constitution, empowering Parliament to legislate on a State subject in national interest, remains in force for a period not exceeding one year. [Article 249 (2)].

stem: Who among the following is empowered to establish the Inter-State council?

The council consists of-Prime Minister - Chairman, Chief Ministers of all states - Members, Chief Ministers of Union Territories having a Legislative Assembly and Administrators of UTs not having a Legislative Assembly - Members, Six ministers of Cabinet rank in the Union Council of Ministers to be nominated by the Prime Minister - Members.

stem: Under which of the following Articles of the Constitution, Inter State Council has been constituted?
expl: The Inter-State Council (ISC) is constituted under Article-263 of the Indian Constitution. It includes the Prime Minister (Head), 6-Central Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers of all the States and Chief Ministers of UTs having a legislative assembly and the Administrators of the Union Territories. The Council is constituted by President by an order. The first ISC was established in May, 1990 and constituted in December, 1990. The Article 365 is - Effect of failure to comply with, or to give effect to, directions given by the Union. The Article 360 is - Provisions as to financial emergency, and the Article 368 contains provisions for the amendment of the Constitution.

options.label: b
options.text: Five Zonal Councils have set up under the State Reorganisation Act, 1956

options.label: c
options.text: Chandigarh although not a state, is included in Zonal Council

expl: The Zonal Councils have been set up under the State Reorganization Act, 1956 to advise on matters of common interest to each of the five zones into which the territory of India has been divided. Zonal Councils are not constitutional bodies rather, they are statutory bodies. Originally, five Zonal Councils were formed as per the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. They are - Northern Zonal Council Central Zonal Council Eastern Zonal Council Western Zonal Council Southern Zonal Council The North Eastern States i.e. (i) Assam (ii) Arunachal Pradesh (iii) Manipur (iv) Tripura (v) Mizoram (vi) Meghalaya and (vii) Nagaland are not included in the zonal council and their special problems are looked after by the North Eastern Council, setup under the North Eastern Council Act, 1971. Chandigarh, although not a state, is included in the zonal council. Similarly Delhi, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu and Puducherry have also been included in the zonal councils.

stem:
The North Eastern Council (NEC) was established by the North Eastern Council Act, 1971. Subsequent to the amendment of NEC Act in 2002, the Council comprises which of the following members?
1. Governor of the Constituent State
2. Chief Minister of the Constituent State
3. Three Members to be nominated by the President of India
4. The Home Minister of India
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
expl: The North Eastern Council (NEC) is the nodal agency for the economic and social development of the North Eastern Region which consists of the eight States of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura. The NEC was established by the North Eastern Council Act, 1971 initially as an apex-level Advisory Body, for securing balanced and coordinated development and facilitating effective co-ordination amongst the seven States of North Eastern Region. Subsequent to the amendment of NEC Act in December, 2002, Sikkim was added as 8th Member State, and the NEC was mandated to function as a statutory Regional Planning Body for the North Eastern Region. As per the amended sub-section (1) of section 3 of the NEC Act, now the Council comprises Governors and Chief Ministers of constituent States as members and three members to be nominated by the President of India. As per the amended sub-section (3) of section 3 of the NEC Act, the President shall nominate the Chairman of the council (and he need not be nominated from amongst the other members). The President may also nominate a member of the council to act as Vice-Chairman of the Council. At present, as nominated by the President (by the notifications dated 7 July, 2018 and 24 August, 2021 respectively), the Union Home Minister is ex-Officio Chairman and the Minister, Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER) is the ex-Officio member and Vice-Chairman of the NEC. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

stem:

Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

options.label: c

expl: The Sarkaria Commission was established in 1983 to consider and give recommendations on Centre-State relations. In its recommendation, the Commission suggested that exercise of Presidential Rule must be in rare or exceptional cases. The Commission had expressed its view that Article 356 had been misused several times. Often, the declaration of President’s Rule was made without considering other provisions. Thus Assertion (A) and Reason (R), are both correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

stem: Which Commission advocated the establishment of a Permanent Inter-State Council, called ‘Inter-Governmental Council?
expl: The Sarkaria Commission recommended the establishment of a Permanent Inter-State Council in its report. On the recommendation of this report, in May, 1990 under Article 263 of the Constitution, by the President's assent, an interstate council was formed that was to be headed by the Prime Minister.

stem: Which one of the the following Commission did recommend the establishment of an Inter- Government Council in place of Inter-State Council?
expl: In order to achieve cooperation between the States and the Centre, Article 263 of the Constitution considers the creation of an Inter-State Council. Therefore, the President may create such a council whenever he feels that doing so would be in the best interests of the general public. The Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State Relations (1983-88) recommended the establishment of a permanent Inter-State Council under Article 263 of the Constitution. It suggested that the Inter-State Council should be referred to as the Inter-Governmental Council to distinguish it from other organisations founded under the same Article 263. In pursuance of the recommendations of the Commission, the Janata Dal Government, headed by V. P. Singh, established the Inter-State Council in 1990. It consists of the following members: (i) Prime minister as the Chairman (ii) Chief ministers of all the states (iii) Chief ministers of union territories having legislative assemblies (iv) Administrators of union territories not having legislative assemblies (v) Governors of States under President’s rule (vi) Six Central cabinet ministers, including the home minister, to be nominated by the Prime Minister. The council is a recommendatory body on issues relating to interstate, Centre-State and Centre-Union territories relations.

stem: On the recommendation of which Commission/ Committee, the Inter-state Council was set up in India?
expl: The Union Government, constituted a Commission in 1983 under the Chairmanship of Justice R.S. Sarkaria to review the working of the existing arrangements between the Union and the States. One of the important recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission was to establish a permanent Inter-State Council as an independent national forum for consultation with a mandate well-defined in accordance with Article 263 of the Constitution of India.

stem:
With reference to India, consider the following :
I. The Inter-State Council
II. The National Security Council
III. Zonal Councils How many of the above were established as per the provisions of the Constitution of India?
expl: The Inter-State Council is envisaged in the Constitution itself under Article 263, Therefore, the Inter-State Council is clearly a body established in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution. The National Security Council (NSC) was set up by an executive decision with the approval of the Prime Minister, not under any specific Article of the Constitution. The Zonal Councils are not established under any Article of the Constitution; rather, they are statutory bodies created through an ordinary Act of Parliament. Only the Inter-State Council falls in the category of “established in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution of India”; hence, the correct option is (a).

stem: Which one of the following is not related to Union-State relations in India?
expl: The Indrajit Gupta Committee was established in 1998 to recommend on state funding of elections, while other three committees were related to Union-State relations in India. The Gupta Committee recommended that state funds should be given to only national and state parties allotted a symbol and not to independent candidates. The commission also suggested that the fund should be given in the form of certain facilities.

stem:

Assertion (A) : There has been a growing demand for a review of Centre-State relationship.

Code :

options.label: b
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are individually true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

expl: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). In the Union of India, the Central Government is more empowered than the State Governments. Although the financial resources are divided between the Centre and States and among States, the Centre has more resources than the States. The States do not have sufficient resources and have to be dependent on Centre. This is why there has been a growing demand for a review of the Centre-State relationship. So option (a) is correct.

stem:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R) :
Assertion (A) : The Executive powers of the State are exercised to ensure the compliance of the law of the Parliament and the laws applied in the State.
Reason (R) : The government of India can give necessary direction to the states by using its executive powers.
Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
Codes :

options.label: a
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: b
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

expl: According to the Article 256, the executive power of every State shall be so exercised as to ensure compliance with the laws made by Parliament and any existing laws which apply in that State, and the executive power of the Union shall extend to the giving of such directions to a State as may appear to the Government of India to be necessary for that purpose. Thus, both statements (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

stem: Which Article of the Indian Constitution describes ‘’The Executive power of every State shall be so exercised as not to impede or prejudice the exercise of the Executive power of the Union.’’
expl: According to Article 257(1) of the Indian Constitution, the executive power of every State shall be so exercised as not to impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union; The executive power of the Union shall extend to giving such direction to States as may appear to the Government of India necessary for that purpose.

stem: Which Part of the Constitution of India describes the financial relations between Centre and States?
expl: Originally, the Indian Constitution had 22 Parts. Some parts are as follows: Part X - The Scheduled and Tribal Areas Part XI - Relations between the Union and the States Part XII - Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits Part XIII - Trade, Commerce and Intercourse within the Territory of India. Thus, the correct answer is option (c).

stem: The financial relations between the Union Government and States have been discussed under –
expl: Distribution of Revenues between the Union Government and States is provided under Article 268 to Article 281 of the Indian Constitution. These articles consist of provisions for Duties and Taxes levied by the Union; Grant-in-aid, constitution and function of the Finance Commission, etc.

stem: Under which Article of the Constitution of India, Taxes are levied and collected by the centre but distributed between the centre and the States?
expl: According to Article 270 of the Indian Constitution, Taxes on income other than agricultural income are levied and collected by the government of India and distributed between the Union and the States.

stem:

2. regulated by the union government

expl: According to Article 268, stamp duty on financial goods deals is imposed by the Union Government but collected and appropriated by the State Government.

stem:
Consider the following statements-In India taxes on transactions in Stock-Exchanges and Futures Markets are –
1. Levied by Union.
2. Collected by the State Government.
Code :
expl: The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution is for the distribution of powers between the Union and the States. There are 3 lists under this- Union List, State List and Concurrent List. According to the question, the tax imposed on the stock market and futures market belongs to the Union List. However, under Article 270 of the Constitution, such taxes are levied and collected by the union but assigned to the states.

stem: Under constitutional provision of tax assignment in India, which of the following is a tax exclusively imposed and collected by the states?
expl: Land Revenue is a tax exclusively imposed and collected by the states. Land Revenue is included in the state list of the seventh schedule of the Indian Constitution under entry 45. Entry 45 includes Land revenue, including the assessment and collection of revenue, the maintenance of land records, surveys for revenue purposes and records of rights and alienation of revenues.

stem: Provision for Descretionary Grant which may be given by Central government to States is given under which Article of the Constitution?
expl: According to the Indian Constitution Article 282 the union or a state may take any grants for any public purpose, notwith standing that the purpose is not one with respect to which parliament or legislature of the state, as the case may be, may make laws.

stem: Is a State of the Indian Union empowered under the Constitution to take foreign loans directly?

options.label: c

options.label: d

expl: According to Article 293 (1), the executive power of a State extends to borrowing within the territory of India upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of the State within such limits, if any, as may from time to time be fixed by the Legislature of such State by law and to the giving of guarantees within such limits. So it is obvious under the Constitution of India that the State cannot obtain foreign loans directly.

stem: Agriculture Income Tax is assigned to the State Government by-

stem: Main agency to resolve the fiscal disputes between the Centre and States is –

The Finance Commission's core responsibility is to recommend the sharing of taxes between the centre and states.

stem: Under which of the following taxes the total amount payable by an individual is limited by the Constitution?

expl: Article 276 (2) of the Constitution specifies that the total amount payable in respect of any person to the State or to any municipality, district board, local board or other local authority in the State by way of taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments shall not exceed two thousand and five hundred rupees (Rs. 2,500) per annum after 60th Amendment Act, 1988 in place of Rs. 250.

stem: Freedom of inter-state trade and commerce has been regulated by the Indian Constitution under Article:
